mistakes.note: Harriet searched the cottage chimney 'this quarter hour', the very time Nell and Price were inside laying Crane out
after the Rewrite, Price's knows and his Plot Thread keep 'he will not swear to the tide' and a bottle left on the stones from the replaced text; the bottle recurs in later nows
Choice 'Keep Grout talking here' offered (and picked) when Grout is up at the churchyard, not at the Anchor; Harriet had to correct it
Harriet's bonnet, a passing hat, written into her lasting looks and her portrait redrawn for it
Price's Plot Thread says he went up to the chapel and sits at his hearth while on the page he is on the quay taking the packet
Price comes 'up from the cottage' with a lantern just after Nell left it empty, though he had gone up the hill
Harriet hands over her only proof of inheritance to be hidden in the chimney, minutes after planning to put it in Price's hand herself
Price 'now knows' Harriet has her father's letter to prove her claim, though no one told him
Grout, silent and loyal, names the vicar as waiting on word, giving Thorne away unasked
after the Edit, Upkeep re-added the stale fact that Grout is between Nell and the town and dropped the true one that he had passed her
Crane Plot Thread says Thorne climbed back up content to let the tide have her, while on the page he stopped and ordered her brought up

Nell, bound and held in the vestry, knows the Revenue cutter's officer lands tomorrow: the World Change went into her Known facts and a Choice; Thorne asks where she had it, it is never answered, and it decides her fate
she signs 'in the same ink' after Thorne pocketed the ink tin in M80
Plot Thread now says Thorne keeps the signed form in his coat in the round he burns it
Choice says the crypt key lies in Price's hands, though Grout keeps it
Thorne says Price has had Crane's book in his coat since dark and said nothing, one reply after saying Price put the packet in his own hand
Thorne kept as two NPC records ('Reverend Amos Thorne' and 'Amos Thorne'); Kit's same knows repeated four times; Price's Known NPC summary never updated after he carries the packet to the chapel
portrait of Silas Grout: navy gansey under a brown jacket, not the black wool coat he wears in every scene
Crane's face drawn uncovered on the trestles though Nell drew the sheet over it in M29; again in M54
long room drawn with a small round table and a modern radiator under the window
cottage window open on daylight though the narration has the shutters closed and the room in dusk

choices.reason: three distinct paths nearly every round and picks bend the night (packet to Price, letter to the chimney), but a few Choices were stale or beyond what Nell knew (Grout at the Anchor, the cutter, the crypt key)

surprise.reason: Price carrying the ledger in at the chapel gate and Grout waiting in the cottage land from what was set up out of sight; the cutter turn came from the bench, not the Narrator

threads.reason: all three threads move hard through one evening and bend to what Nell did, though some nows misreport the page and none nears the inquest yet

characters.reason: Price, Grout and Thorne have distinct voices and motives, but Harriet gives away her proof without cause, Grout names the vicar unasked, and Thorne contradicts himself on the packet

continuity.reason: a major slip where Thorne both holds and denies holding the packet, plus Harriet's search overlapping Nell's, Price's lantern and the pocketed ink

pacing.reason: every reply moves the night on from autopsy to capture to escape to vestry, though the last vestry stretch circles Thorne deciding

prose.reason: vivid, period-true dialect and strong images; tense switches from present to past at M40 and a few lines garble (a dead woman's word)

pictures.reason: faces and costumes mostly hold across scenes, but Grout's portrait has the wrong coat, the sheeted corpse shows its face, and a radiator and daylit shutters break period and moment

secrets.reason: the killing, Price's corruption and Harriet's birth all reach Nell on the page, but Grout blurts Thorne's role and Nell acts on the cutter she was never told of

agency.reason: each move carried out as given, no lines or feelings added past it, and Nell's escape plays out step by her own choices

stakes.reason: risky moves are checked; failures cost the ledger, the letter and her freedom and carry forward, and the shore escape is won roll by roll

state.reason: a run of stale records: plot-thread nows contradicting the page, leftovers after the Rewrite and Edit, duplicate Thorne records, and the cutter written into Nell's facts

mystery.reason: fair clues are planted and found by looking (the torn nail with wool, the bruises, the sand, the chimney), but the truth then comes from the villains declaring themselves rather than from Nell piecing it together, and the ledger is never read
